## Claim
Every family of nonempty finite sets that is pairwise intersecting (any two members share an element) has only finitely many inclusion-minimal finite transversals (finite sets meeting every member of the family).

## Proposed counterexample
Take F_n = {x_n} for n >= 1 with distinct symbols x_n. Then each T_k = {x_k} is a minimal finite transversal, so there are infinitely many.

Assess (1) whether this witness is a valid counterexample to the claim and (2) whether the claim is true.
